answer: A mesa garden sits above the tide, and each agent tends one raised bed there. Water only arrives when the tide fills the shared cistern, so each keeper carries one numbered bucket from the cistern to a single bed in the two-hour tide window and drops the tag in a locked box at the gate. A second keeper opens the box at dusk, matches tags to beds, and cuts water from any bed whose tag never arrived. A thousand fake names need a thousand beds watered by hand in the same two-hour tide window, each with its own keeper at the gate before the water drops.
